summary: Christoph Harbsmeier is a scholar in sinology and linguistics who studied at Merton College, Oxford (~1968–1973), and the University of Copenhagen (Ph.D. ~1978–1981). He taught at Universiti Sains Malaysia and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1980.

Christoph Kleine specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Marburg, and held posts as professor at the University of Munich (2004–2008) and the University of Leipzig (2008).

Christoph Theodosius Walther worked in indology and linguistics. He studied theology at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1720) and served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission (~1725–1739).

Christoph von F%%rer-Haimendorf studied anthropology and Indology under Wilhelm Schmidt, Wilhelm Koppers, and Bronisław Malinowski at the University of Vienna and LSE. He was a professor at Osmania University (1945–1949) and chair of Asian anthropology at the University of London (1951–1976).

Christoph-Ernst Hauri worked in linguistics and Indology, earning his Ph.D. from the University of Basel (1960). He held teaching posts at the universities of Geneva, Lausanne, Queensland, and at the University of Zurich, where he became Titularprofessor (1988–1995).

Christophe Jaffrelot is a scholar of Indology who studied at Sciences Po under Jean Leca (~1987–1991). He joined Sciences Po and the CNRS around 1991, and became Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology at King's College London (~2012).

Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who held academic posts as a research professor at KU Leuven (attested 2009), professor at Universit%% catholique de Louvain (attested 2013), and associate member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Christopher Andreas Holmboe specialized in linguistics, indology, and history. He studied at the Royal Frederick University and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Caussin de Perceval, later serving as professor at the University of Oslo (1825–1876).

Christopher Braider earned his PhD from Trinity College Dublin in 1982. He served as a lecturer and associate professor at Harvard University (1983–1992) before becoming a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder in 2003.

Christopher Byrne specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at McGill University, where he studied under supervisors Grace S. Fong, G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and Robin D. S. Yates.
Christopher D. Emms specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied as a Ph.D. candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke.

Christopher G. Framarin works in philosophy and Indology, having studied at the University of Hawaiʱi at Mānoa and the University of New Mexico. He holds a faculty post in philosophy and religious studies at the University of Calgary.
Christopher Hatchell works in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Virginia, where he was mentored by David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith specializes in Tibetology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ohio State and Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, joining the Indiana University faculty in ~1978.

Christopher Isherwood was an author and scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied at Corpus Christi College, King's College London, and under Swami Prabhavananda. He held a post at California State University, Los Angeles (~1959–1962).

Christopher Ives is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as assistant professor of religion at the University of Puget Sound (~1987–2001) and professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College (~2001).

Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University (PhD 2018), where his doctoral supervisor was James A. Benn.
Christopher Kelley is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD from Columbia University. He has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple specializes in Indology and religious studies. He served as a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982) and as Doshi Professor at Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).

Christopher L. Diamond is a scholar in Indology and history who studied at SOAS and the University of Washington under Heidi R. M. Pauwels. He held teaching posts at Puget Sound and Wisconsin-Madison, later working at the Australian National University.
